verbatim_locators.note: COVERAGE: whole article read including Table 1 and Figure 1 as an image. REVIEW: no experimental data of its own; every number is a restatement of a cited primary and was NOT checked against those primaries (refs 9, 43, 46, 53, 55, 63, 71, 79 identified). WWOX does not occur in the article (term count 0), so the review establishes a base rate for KD across DEE aetiologies and nothing about WWOX.

entries.proposition: DESIGN: a narrative, non-systematic review with a search closing at January 2024; no quantitative synthesis, no quality appraisal. It is a secondary source.
entries.snippet: this review presents a qualitative, narrative synthesis rather than a quantitative meta-analysis

entries.proposition: The gene-wise responder rates the review gives (SCN1A, KCNQ2, STXBP1, SCN2A) come from very small cohorts, a single study (its ref 9) behind all four, with n of 18, 6, 4 and 3.
entries.anchor: 5.6 DEE associated with other genetic mutations

entries.proposition: The one gene-level negative: CDKL5-related DEE, 0 of 10 responders in the same small study, and a registry of 104 with improvement in 61 of the 69 who changed but poor long-term efficacy. KD response is therefore heterogeneous by gene, from 0 to 100 percent in cohorts of 3 to 18.
entries.snippet: one small study reported no significant response (n = 10, responder rate = 0.0%, p = 0.031)

entries.proposition: Syndrome-level prior for infantile spasms: spasm cessation in 23 of 43 children.
entries.snippet: KD successfully terminated seizures in 53.5% (23/43) of children

entries.proposition: Syndrome-level prior for Dravet syndrome with attrition: the 50 percent responder fraction falls from 63 to 47 percent between 3 and 12 months.
entries.snippet: seizure reduction ≥50% was observed in 63%, 60%, and 47% of patients at 3, 6, and 12 months, respectively

entries.proposition: Syndrome-level prior for Lennox-Gastaut: 47 percent with at least a 50 percent seizure reduction in 189 children.
entries.snippet: In a cohort of 189 children with LGS, 47% achieved ≥50% seizure reduction after 3–36 months of KD therapy

entries.proposition: The Outlook states KD reduces or controls seizures in "most" DEE cases, a sentence stronger than the syndrome figures the review itself gives (47 to 63 percent responder fractions at the 50 percent threshold) and silent on how responders were defined across studies.
entries.snippet: KD not only reduces or controls seizures in most DEE cases

entries.proposition: SELECTION: KD is introduced after multiple drugs and even surgery have failed, so any responder fraction describes a refractory, pre-selected population.
entries.snippet: KD is commonly introduced after the failure of multiple antiseizure medications and even epilepsy surgery

entries.proposition: MECHANISM: the review lists ketone-body mechanisms (glutamate down, GABA up, mitochondrial ATP, adenosine, histone deacetylase inhibition, cytokines, microbiota, PUFAs) and says the precise mechanisms are not established; energy repletion and Warburg reversal are not distinguished.
entries.snippet: Although the precise mechanisms are not yet fully elucidated, the clinical efficacy of KD is widely recognized

entries.proposition: Figure 1 is a pathway schematic (seven bands: direct action, neurotransmitter regulation, anti-inflammatory, gut microbiota, PUFAs); it carries no data and no WWOX-relevant node.
entries.snippet: [figure attestation - pixels cannot be quote-matched] Figure 1, schematic with bands Direct action, Neurotransmitter regulation, Anti-inflammatory and immune, The impact of gut microbiota, PUFAs, each leading to Anti-epileptic; legend "Putative anticonvulsant mechanisms of the ketogenic diet".

entries.proposition: HYPOGLYCAEMIA AT INITIATION: hypoglycaemia and dehydration are named as common early adverse effects, related to fasting and reduced intake.
entries.snippet: Common early adverse effects of KD include hypoglycemia and dehydration, typically related to fasting and reduced caloric intake

entries.proposition: In 12-month-old-or-younger infants on KD only two children had significant hypoglycaemia at initiation (due to vomiting and poor intake).
entries.snippet: Only two children experienced significant hypoglycemia at initiation due to vomiting and reduced oral intake

entries.proposition: CONTRAINDICATIONS: mitochondrial respiratory chain disorders and fatty-acid oxidation defects are contraindications; any mitochondrial-dysfunction reading of WWOX loss would collide with them.
entries.snippet: mitochondrial respiratory chain disorders, and severe hepatic or pancreatic dysfunction

entries.proposition: The review names KD first-line for GLUT1 deficiency and pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency, the two energy-supply defects.
entries.snippet: It is considered a first-line treatment for metabolic epilepsies such as GLUT1 deficiency syndrome and pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency

entries.proposition: The authors state the evidence base is limited in sample size and follow-up.
entries.snippet: Due to limitations in sample size and follow-up duration, further studies are required to evaluate the long-term safety and efficacy of KD
